stories.head: Drones threaten U.S. rocket launch schedules
stories.body: Recent reports indicate that drone activity around U.S. rocket launch sites is becoming increasingly disruptive, with one misfired UAV potentially costing millions in delays for multiple launch providers. This uptick in drone threats adds a layer of complexity to an already fraught launch environment, where timing is everything. Companies may need to invest more in counter-drone technologies to protect their assets.
stories.soWhat: If rocket companies don’t adapt quickly, they might find themselves grounded—literally.

stories.head: EchoStar's subsidiaries file for Chapter 11
stories.body: EchoStar's satellite TV and wireless subsidiaries have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a strategic restructuring plan after selling spectrum to SpaceX and AT&T. This move underscores the shifting landscape of the satellite industry, where traditional models are increasingly challenged. The restructuring could allow EchoStar to refocus on more viable business lines, but it also raises questions about the sustainability of satellite TV.
stories.soWhat: The satellite TV model is looking more like a relic than a revenue generator.

stories.head: Latitude plans first launch from Oman in 2027
stories.body: French startup Latitude has announced plans for its inaugural launch from Oman, targeting late 2027 for the event. This marks a significant step for Oman as it aims to establish itself as a new player in the space launch market. With the global launch landscape becoming increasingly competitive, Latitude's choice of location could offer strategic advantages in terms of access and cost.
stories.soWhat: If successful, this could be the beginning of a new launch hub that reshapes regional dynamics.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
